source_reviews.independent_solution: Reuse d280: from the front-wall side hole, the beam in clean air is not visible in the intended negligible-visible-scattering model, because the unredirected beam travels between the side-wall holes rather than into the eye. Clean does not imply literally zero scattering; sufficiently strong side scattering or a different observation path can alter visibility. A lit wall/hole is not the beam path in air.

coverage.evidence: New /0/options/0 now gives the missing conditional nonvisibility prediction, explicitly tied to the front-hole side view, negligible visible scattering, no stray reflections and an eye off the direct side-hole path. It does not assert those model conditions as measured facts about all clean air.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Reuse d280: a Sun-viewing observer inside the lunar penumbra sees a partial solar eclipse. Some, not all, rays from the extended solar disk are intercepted by the Moon. Merely having some part of Earth in that region does not place every terrestrial observer there.

coverage.evidence: Visible /1 A retains the local partial-disk prediction; C separates an unlocated observer from the Earth-overall statement. The additional location distinction supports rather than substitutes for the eclipse task.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Reuse d280: an effective small aperture produces a camera-obscura scene image by near-straight rays crossing at the opening; upper/lower and left/right object coordinates reverse on the opposite screen. An opening small in both transverse directions supports a resolved two-dimensional scene; a long unrestricted slit need not. Colors can come from the illuminated objects' own reflected light. A literal dispersed spectrum is not established by the literary rainbow description.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Reuse d280: a finite emitting region gives displaced shadow edges and a penumbra. Feet are near the ground screen, so displacement is small; the head is farther from that screen, so penumbra broadens. For the same local finite-source geometry, w approximately equals D b/a. An ideal point source has no source-size penumbra.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Reuse d280, without rerunning its arithmetic: 1.6 m from 80 cd and 2.0 m from 125 cd; normal direct illuminance is 31.25 lx per opposite face. At cosine zero, both ideal direct illuminances vanish at every interior position and equality is nonunique.

mathematics.independent_solution: In the d280 small-aperture geometric model, a ray through the opening at the origin from an object point of height y at positive object distance u reaches a wall at positive image distance v with image height -(v/u)y. The analogous horizontal coordinate also reverses. A is a qualified possible path, not an unconditional sharp-image claim for every gap. A lens is unnecessary: a pinhole is a counterexample to B. Colored scene light can form a colored image without a disperser, falsifying C's claimed sufficiency and supporting D.

option_checks.evidence: For a sufficiently direction-limiting aperture, near-straight continuation through the opening maps an upper object point to a lower wall point. The option says if/can; it does not assert this resolution for every unspecified slit.
A small pinhole and an opposite screen produce an inverted object image with no lens. This supplies a direct counterexample to the option's impossibility.
A pinhole imaging differently colored objects yields a colored picture without splitting white light into a spectrum. Thus rainbow-like colors alone do not establish dispersion as its cause.
The objects' reflected spectral distributions can remain distinguishable through the opening. Their spatial image colors do not require a prism, grating or other white-light disperser.

Finite source points give different projected edges; the short foot-to-ground distance yields a narrow penumbra, and the larger head-to-ground distance yields a wider one.
Changing b/a changes the separation of the finite-source edge projections and hence penumbra width, not only overall shadow size.
